name: Pontypool water-powered sheet rolling
description: At a Pontypool ironworks, water-driven rollers reduced iron bars to sheet used for household ironware.

date.label: 1697 observer’s account
date.basis: Date describes the reported event or archaeological context, not the origin of the general technique.

events.statement: The report reproduces Edward Lhwyd’s 1697 account of water-driven rollers and ironware made from the resulting sheet.

evidence.supports: The report reproduces Edward Lhwyd’s 1697 account of water-driven rollers and ironware made from the resulting sheet.

earliest_record.rationale: First researched event for this local case; it does not establish worldwide priority.

caveats: An observer’s quoted report; dates the account rather than the onset of rolling. The stated price compares finished vessels, not the cost of iron or machinery.

research.note: Independent review checked the 1697 quoted observer account and its comparison of finished-vessel prices.

measures.conditions: Lhwyd’s 1697 claim for Hanbury’s finished vessels; denominator is an unspecified usual price, not manufacturing cost.
